answer: Each epoch the protocol assigns every identity one random peer to audit, and the auditor locks a 25-credit bond that is burned if that peer is later proven a duplicate. A clone farm cannot audit itself for free: every fake identity still needs a separate, economically exposed auditor, so 1,000 clones put 25,000 credits at risk each cycle. Like a river cutting one fixed channel, the cost flows only to the attacker; an honest agent audits a single peer, reclaims the bond, and pays nothing, and no spiral of wandering fake accounts can wash it away.
